OTF (Only The Family) is a Chicago-based rap collective and record label founded by rapper Lil Durk. The collective became a major name in Chicago’s drill music scene, helping introduce artists such as King Von, Booka600, & Memo600 to wider audiences. OTF is known for its strong Chicago roots, distinctive sound, & influence on modern hip-hop culture.

Lil Durk, whose real name is Durk Derrick Banks, is a Chicago rapper, singer, and songwriter who rose to fame during the early 2010s drill movement. Known for blending melodic rap with storytelling about his upbringing and personal experiences, Durk became one of the biggest names in hip-hop. His catalog includes major projects like 7220 and Almost Healed, along with collaborations with Drake, Lil Baby, & J. Cole.

SOB X RBE (Strictly Only Brothers X Real Boi Entertainment) is a legendary Bay Area rap group from Vallejo, California, best known for its high-energy music, aggressive delivery, and undeniable chemistry. The group rose to national fame in the late 2010s with members Yhung T.O., DaBoii, Slimmy B, and Lul G. They gained widespread attention with records like “Anti,” “Carpoolin’,” & “Paramedic!,” which appeared on the Black Panther soundtrack.

After nearly seven years apart, SOB X RBE is experiencing a major comeback in 2026. Yhung T.O., DaBoii, and Slimmy B reunited and have been going viral across social media, with fans celebrating their return & revisiting their classic hits. Viral moments involving their signature “Blame Em” dance, appearances at a San Francisco 49ers game, and interactions with streamer DDG have helped bring renewed attention to the group. The group recently kicked off its highly anticipated From The Land Tour on November 4 in Ventura, followed by performances in San Luis Obispo, Santa Ana, & SD. They also released their first group album in seven years, From The Land, on 11/6, featuring 13 tracks. With more West Coast performances scheduled, including appearances at the SAP Center in San Jose and Golden 1 Center in Sac, SOB X RBE is proving that its influence on Bay Area rap is still going strong.
